article.headline: Central Texas braces for 4-6 inches of rain as flooding risk peaks Thursday
article.summary: A Flood Watch covering most of Central Texas through Friday evening brings multiple rounds of storms with 2-4 inches of rain expected, rising to 4-6 inches in isolated areas, with the highest flooding risk on Thursday.
article.body:
Central Texas faces a moderate to high risk of street, flash, and river flooding on Thursday as tropical moisture collides with a slow-moving front and low pressure system to fuel multiple rounds of downpours. Most of Central Texas is under a Flood Watch from Wednesday evening through Friday evening, according to FOX 7 Austin.

The forecast danger peaks Thursday with two distinct storm rounds. The first arrives early in the day with scattered storms and moderate rain, while a second round of widespread heavy rain and strong storms follows late Thursday, bringing the main flooding concern along with small hail and gusty winds. The slow-moving front will focus storm development, and upper-level lift will keep storms strong throughout the period.

Rainfall totals of 2-4 inches are expected across the region, but isolated areas will receive 4-6 inches. Where the highest totals occur remains the biggest forecasting challenge. North Texas faces a similar multi-day wet pattern, with a separate Flood Watch extended through 7 a.m. Friday, bringing widespread totals of 2-4 inches and isolated amounts of 5-6 inches, according to FOX 4 News Dallas-Fort Worth. The exceptionally dry ground in the North Texas region will increase rapid runoff and localized flooding risk, especially where storms train over the same areas overnight and into Thursday morning.

A cold front will move through Friday, bringing relief from the unseasonable heat with highs dropping into the upper 70s and lower 80s by late week.

article.headline: Trump adviser tells Canadian lobbyists to 'get the hell out' of U.S.
article.summary: Peter Navarro, a trade adviser to President Trump, warned Canadian lobbyists on Tuesday to leave the U.S. and threatened repercussions if Canada interferes in upcoming midterm elections.
article.body:
Peter Navarro, one of U.S. President Donald Trump's trade advisers, issued a direct threat to Canada during remarks at an economic conference in Washington on Tuesday. "Memo to Canada: You cannot do that," Navarro said, telling Canadian lobbyists on K Street—Washington's hub for lobbying firms—to "get the hell out of our country" and warning that "if you interfere in our elections in Maine or Michigan you will pay even more dearly."

Navarro's comments signal escalating friction over Canada's approach to U.S. trade policy. He criticized Ottawa's strategy of leaning on American labor and business groups to influence negotiations, a tactic Canada used during talks that led to the Canada-U.S.-Mexico Agreement in Trump's first term. Since Trump returned to the White House in early 2025, Canadian provinces have also hired representatives to advocate for their interests during ongoing trade discussions in Washington.

The tensions come as a U.S. ban on certain Canadian imports took effect at midnight on Tuesday, affecting key industries including alcohol, dairy, and motorcycles. Trump signed the executive order in response to Canada's retaliatory tariffs following the collapse of trade talks in August. The White House justified the measure by saying Canada's restrictions on U.S. alcohol, autos, and dairy products put American exporters at a disadvantage.

When asked about Navarro's remarks at a press conference in Vancouver, Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney laughed and said he had "no response" to the warning. Navarro said he "loves" the Canadian people but has harbored no goodwill toward Canadian negotiators since 2016.

article.headline: Steelers trade cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to Cowboys after failed contract extension talks
article.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers traded cornerback Joey Porter Jr. to the Dallas Cowboys on Wednesday after the two sides could not reach a contract extension agreement, with Porter in the final year of his rookie deal at a $4.9 million cap hit.
article.body:
Joey Porter Jr. has not played a snap this season for Pittsburgh, sitting out the first three games after being placed on the reserve/non-injury list in early August with a back injury that many believed masked a deeper contractual dispute.

For the Steelers, the trade represents a reset after months of failed negotiations. General manager Omar Khan had stated in late August that the franchise would not negotiate extensions during the season, and no deal materialized before Pittsburgh's Week 1 deadline. Steelers coach Mike McCarthy acknowledged the two sides were at an "impasse" in talks. Porter, drafted 32nd overall in 2023, wanted compensation matching top-tier cornerbacks—Christian Gonzalez signed a four-year, $135 million deal this offseason and Devon Witherspoon a four-year, $132 million contract—but Pittsburgh declined to match those figures.

For Dallas, the trade accelerates the Cowboys' defensive overhaul. The team started last season by acquiring Kenny Clark and Quinnen Williams, then added Rashan Gary before the draft. The secondary has struggled early this season after losing Cobie Durant to injury, and Dallas enters the trade with a 1-2 record. Adding Porter addresses that weakness as the franchise attempts to improve pass protection.

Porter's three-year NFL resume includes 165 combined tackles, 3 interceptions, and 31 passes defended. Last season he appeared in 14 games with 52 tackles, one sack, one interception, and 14 passes defended. His father, Joey Porter, played linebacker in the NFL from 1999 to 2011 with Pittsburgh, Miami, and Arizona.

article.headline: Green ID book production ends March 31, 2027, then banned next year
article.summary: South Africa's Home Affairs Minister announced the green ID book will stop being produced on March 31, 2027, and will no longer be valid identification from March 31, 2028, as the government shifts to the more secure Smart ID card.
article.body:
The green ID book's 12-month countdown to obsolescence begins when production shuts down on 31 March 2027. From 31 March 2028, the document will no longer be recognised as valid identification, giving millions of South Africans a year to switch to the Smart ID card or the newly demonstrated digital ID credential.

Home Affairs Minister Leon Schreiber cited security as the driving force. Independent research found the green ID book is among Africa's most fraud-prone identity documents because it relies on paper and manual photographs that can be manipulated. Schreiber said the document "sits at the core of the scourge of identity theft in the country" and enables the production of fraudulent papers, including those used by people seeking illegal South African documentation.

On the same day Schreiber announced the green ID deadline, he demonstrated South Africa's first working digital ID on his smartphone, using the MyMzansi app and his thumbprint to confirm his identity. The digital credential displays the photograph from the population register rather than a model image. Director-general Tommy Makhode tested the system by requesting Schreiber's citizenship details; Schreiber generated a QR code that Makhode scanned, then selectively shared his nationality while blocking his ID number. The digital ID is set to be voluntary, though no launch date has been announced.

article.headline: Disruptive passenger triggers 2-hour delay, passengers applaud as woman exits Scoot flight
article.summary: A woman was removed from Scoot flight TR905 in Macau on September 27 for disruptive behaviour, causing a two-hour delay before the plane departed for Singapore with 173 passengers.
article.body:
As the woman was led off the aircraft by police and flight attendants, passengers applauded in the background. She raised her hands with peace signs while being escorted down the aisle by at least four security personnel.

The disruption cost the flight significantly: flight TR905 was scheduled to depart Macau for Singapore at 6.45pm local time but did not leave until 8.46pm. According to Scoot, the delay stemmed from the time required to remove the disruptive passenger, wait for local authorities to arrive, and offload her checked baggage. All 173 other passengers remained on the aircraft and were served refreshments during the two-hour wait.

Scoot handed the passenger over to local authorities at Macau International Airport but did not disclose what disturbance she had caused on board. The Straits Times reported the incident occurred on October 1, while other sources place the flight on September 27 and the video posting on September 28. Investigations into the incident are ongoing, Scoot said, unable to provide further details. The airline apologised and stated that "the safety and well-being of our customers and crew are our top priority and we will take appropriate measures against any passenger who poses a risk to them."

article.headline: 4-0 rout sends Argentina into post-Messi era with emphatic Cordoba victory
article.summary: Argentina defeated Bolivia 4-0 in a friendly in Cordoba, with goals from Lautaro Martinez, Nico Paz, Cristian Romero, and Jose Lopez, marking the team's first match since Lionel Messi announced his international retirement.
article.body:
Argentina hammered Bolivia 4-0 at Estadio Mario Alberto Kempes in Cordoba, dominating a friendly that marked the start of the post-Messi era. Lautaro Martinez opened the scoring in the 19th minute with a drilled finish, followed by Nico Paz's dink to make it 2-0. Cristian Romero headed in Argentina's third from Paz's free-kick in the 54th minute, before Jose Lopez added a late fourth from the bench after initially seeing a strike ruled offside for his maiden Argentina goal.

The emphatic victory comes as Argentina moves forward without Lionel Messi, who recently confirmed his international retirement. Coach Lionel Scaloni praised the integration of fresh talent, expressing emotion about giving debuts to young players. Scaloni highlighted the joy of watching debutants sing the national anthem and specifically commended Jose Lopez for his pressing work rate, tactical movement, and professional attitude.

Argentina's dominance was overwhelming. They had 18 attempts to Bolivia's three shots, none of which were on target. Expected goals favored Argentina 2.24 to Bolivia's 0.11, underscoring their control throughout. Nico Paz and Alcaraz led with three shots each, while Martinez recorded seven touches in the opponent's box. Paz also crafted three chances, joint-leading with Franco Mastantuono, another young talent helping fill the void left by Messi's departure.

With Messi no longer part the setup, much of the attacking responsibility now falls on Martinez, Paz, and Julian Alvarez. Argentina will face Benin next week, which will serve as a farewell match for the eight-time Ballon d'Or winner, though tougher tests lie ahead for Scaloni's reconstructed team.

article.headline: Justice Department files ethics complaint against 7 Minnesota judges over immigration enforcement comments
article.summary: Attorney General Todd Blanche announced the DOJ filed a judicial misconduct complaint Wednesday against seven federal judges in Minnesota who spoke to the New York Times about government violations of court orders during Operation Metro Surge.
article.body:
The Justice Department took the unusual step of filing a complaint with the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 8th Circuit against judges who publicly discussed their concerns over the Trump administration's immigration enforcement surge. At the center of the dispute is a New York Times article featuring Judge Patrick Schiltz, who gave a 90-minute interview describing what he said were repeated violations of court orders by the government. Schiltz, nominated by President George W. Bush and a former law clerk to Supreme Court Justice Antonin Scalia, accused the government in January of failing to comply with nearly 100 court orders and wrote in a ruling that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement "is not a law unto itself."

Attorney General Todd Blanche argued the judges violated judicial ethics and showed bias in their remarks. "When we have a situation like we have now, where you have a judge, a couple of judges, just not only violating the canons in our view, but also showing bias in what they're saying, we have no choice but to act to defend not only our prosecutors, but also DHS," Blanche said at a press conference.

The complaint names Schiltz and Judge John Tunheim, nominated by President Bill Clinton, along with anonymous district judges serving on the U.S. District Court for the District of Minnesota. Six of the seven members of Minnesota's federal bench spoke with the New York Times about Operation Metro Surge, which led to thousands of arrests in the Twin Cities during last winter.

The DOJ is demanding the judges recuse themselves from all criminal and civil cases involving the Department of Homeland Security. However, a Minnesota federal court spokesperson told the Associated Press that legal experts have stated the judges acted "well within the ethical rules that apply to federal judges" in their comments to the newspaper.

article.headline: Perth Police Snatch Power to Ban Protesters From Defence Expo Fort
article.summary: Western Australian police are enforcing a strict security zone at next week's Land Forces expo, with letters already issued banning specific individuals from the site.
article.body:
Letters delivered to at least six people this week warn that entering the designated security zone around the Perth Convention and Exhibition Centre will result in arrest, a maximum of three years in prison, and fines up to $36,000. These restrictions are part of a fortified security operation that includes the use of facial recognition technology to track those on an exclusion list. Protesters who remain on the list are legally required to stay outside the perimeter, which covers the exhibition centre and the Elizabeth Quay bus port.

These measures represent a significant shift in event management for Western Australia, as the state government aims to avoid the violent clashes that occurred during the 2024 Land Forces expo in Melbourne, where 24 police officers were injured by protesters throwing items including rocks and acid. To facilitate the event, which runs from October 6 to 8 and is expected to host 20,000 delegates, the government has allocated $11.5 million for enhanced security.

Under new legislation passed last month, police now possess broad temporary powers until October 10. Within the security zone, officers are authorized to stop, search, and evict any person, as well as remove face coverings. The list of items police can confiscate is extensive, ranging from speakers and microphones to dangerous insects like bees, flares, and bottles. While Commander Darren Seivwright confirmed the operation creates a secure fort, groups including the Greens and the WA Anti-War Collective have criticized the police for a lack of transparency regarding the criteria for the bans.

The security zone remains in effect until October 10 to cover the full duration of the event, including the setup and final pack-down phases.

article.headline: Suzuki beat Miller's slider for walk-off; Padres' closer eyes revenge in playoff rematch
article.summary: Chicago Cubs outfielder Seiya Suzuki hit a walk-off single off San Diego Padres closer Mason Miller on a slider in June, but the two face off again Tuesday in the Wild Card Series with the Cubs' season at stake.
article.body:
Seiya Suzuki has already solved Mason Miller once this year, and now he may get another chance to do it when it counts most. On June 29 at Wrigley Field, Suzuki faced Miller with two outs and the score tied 2-2 in the ninth inning. Miller had entered after two Cubs reached base, and a double play at the plate had nearly ended Chicago's chance. Suzuki drove a slider toward left-field ivy for a walk-off single, scoring Crow-Armstrong for a 3-2 victory.

Miller's regular-season dominance suggests that single may prove the exception rather than the rule. The Padres closer finished the season with 38 saves, establishing himself as one of baseball's most dominant ninth-inning pitchers. His 102.9 mph fastball has overpowered most hitters, including Suzuki in last year's playoffs.

The Cubs will open their Wild Card Series against the Padres on Tuesday at Petco Park, with Michael King starting for San Diego but Miller likely taking over in crucial late-inning situations. Suzuki's June success came when he specifically looked for a slider while remaining aware of Miller's triple-digit fastball. He let the first slider go above the zone, then drove the next one that came over the heart of the plate. Whether Miller repeats that mistake remains unclear, but their rematch could prove decisive with Chicago's season hanging in the balance.

article.headline: Luke Woodhouse stuns world number one Luke Littler at World Grand Prix
article.summary: Defending champion Luke Littler suffered a 2-1 first-round loss to Luke Woodhouse on Monday at the 2026 World Grand Prix in Leicester.
article.body:
World number one Luke Littler saw his World Grand Prix title defense end in the opening round after a 2-1 defeat by Luke Woodhouse. The 19-year-old opened the match by winning the first set 3-1, including a 106 checkout on double 15. However, Woodhouse rallied to win the second set and held his nerve on a double 16 in the decider to force a final set. Woodhouse moved 2-0 ahead in the last set and sealed the victory on double 12, with both players averaging near 82.50 across the match.

For followers of the Professional Darts Corporation, the tournament remains a high-stakes event with a total prize fund of £750,000, representing a 25% increase from the previous year. The tournament is unique for its 'double in, double out' format, which has been in place since 1998 and requires players to start every leg on a double. The winner of the overall event stands to take home £150,000, up from the £120,000 awarded in 2025.

According to The Guardian, this result comes following a week of scrutiny for Littler, who recently faced negative crowd reactions during a tournament in the Netherlands. Despite the loss, the world number one publicly congratulated Woodhouse on his performance via social media. The field for this year's competition comprises 32 players, including the top 16 ranked in the PDC Order of Merit and 16 others who qualified over the past 12 months.

Woodhouse now advances to the last 16 stage of the tournament. He is scheduled to face Nathan Aspinall, who reached this round by defeating Kevin Doets 2-1. The event continues in Leicester as the remaining competitors vie for the increased prize purse.

article.headline: Piastri's brake lock-up in Azerbaijan drops him from podium to points-free horror
article.summary: Oscar Piastri locked up on lap 40 of the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, plummeting from third place to 14th and out of the points in what he called a surprising moment that extended his difficult 2026 season.
article.body:
Piastri held second place through the opening corner of the Baku race, overtaking Charles Leclerc and holding off Max Verstappen's early pressure. He maintained position through the first safety car restart but lost ground to Verstappen before a second safety car reset the field. On the 40th lap, defending his third position against Isack Hadjar at Turn 1, both of Piastri's front brakes locked up simultaneously, sending him off the track and down the order in a single moment.

The incident wiped out what would have been Piastri's first podium since Miami in May. Instead of scoring points, he finished 14th, his second consecutive race without a result. McLaren scored no points in Azerbaijan, with teammate Lando Norris also failing to score after a collision at the opening corner.

Piastri said the lock-up "certainly took me by surprise," telling reporters he did not brake late or hard before both fronts locked. "I didn't think I braked super late or super hard – just instantly locked both fronts, so I need to look at that," he said, noting he would review the data to understand whether a bump in the road or another factor caused the failure.

The setback extends Piastri's difficult 2026 season, in which he has scored just two podiums so far. Norris has taken two wins in the previous five races, widening the gap between the teammates.

article.headline: Abdul Samad smashes 22 off five balls as Pakistan reach first Asian Games cricket final
article.summary: Pakistan defeated Bangladesh by six wickets on October 1 to reach their maiden Asian Games cricket final, where they will face India on October 3 for the gold medal.
article.body:
Abdul Samad's explosive 22 runs off just five balls in the 10th over turned the semi-final decisively Pakistan's way. The match was effectively decided in that single over, bowled by Bangladesh's Mustafizur Rahman, when Pakistan still needed 36 runs from 24 balls.

Pakistan's place in their first-ever Asian Games cricket final ends a long wait for the men's team. They will now face world champions India on October 3 for the gold medal, after India dismantled Sri Lanka by 124 runs in the other semi-final on the same day.

Bangladesh had posted 111-7 after Pakistan asked them to bat on a heavily cracked pitch at Korogi Athletic Park Stadium in Nagoya. Pakistan's bowlers had Bangladesh reeling at 21-3 and then 45-4 in the sixth over. Towhid Hridoy led a recovery with 42 off 25 balls with two fours and four sixes. Pakistan lost three early wickets chasing quick runs but recovered from 53-4 when Samad and Hasan Nawaz came together. The pair posted an unbroken 59-run stand in 32 balls as Pakistan cruised home with nine balls to spare.

Pakistan batsman Saim Ayub, who scored 21, said: "All we care about is winning the final, no matter who we are playing against."

article.summary: Director Danny Boyle endorsed actor Jack O'Connell as the next James Bond during a masterclass at the Zurich Film Festival, praising his ability to make audiences root for morally complex characters.
article.body:
At the Zurich Film Festival, Danny Boyle made his pitch for the next 007: Jack O'Connell. The 28 Years Later director, who was once attached to direct Bond 25 before it became No Time To Die, believes O'Connell has the range to carry the spy franchise. Boyle highlighted O'Connell's performance in the 2024 film Ink, where he plays Larry Lamb, a British tabloid editor, describing how the actor makes audiences remain invested in a character whose moral conscience dissolves entirely as he pursues success.

Boyle's endorsement carries weight given his experience with Bond films. He drew comparisons between O'Connell's work in Ink and Al Pacino's performance in The Godfather Part II, suggesting the actor possesses the complexity needed for the iconic role. The director also referenced O'Connell's recent work in the Amy Winehouse biopic Back To Black, calling it "an incredible performance" in "an impossible part."

The casting search for the next James Bond has stretched on as Amazon pursues the rights to the franchise. Boyle's public endorsement adds O'Connell's name to a growing list of candidates who have been suggested for the role, which requires an actor capable of handling both the action and the psychological depth the character demands.

During the same festival appearance, Boyle confirmed that the third film in the 28 Years Later trilogy will be made, with a script by Alex Garland already completed, though timing remains uncertain.

Each of the four pairs must survive on a tight budget of just £26 per person a day, navigating through prehistoric jungles and five check points across three countries and two continents without the use of phones, credit cards, or flights.

This grueling adventure matters to viewers as it strips away the VIP lifestyle, forcing household names to rely entirely on local transport, maps, and the kindness of strangers. The experience is designed to test emotional resilience and transform relationships as contestants trade home comforts for an environment where they must manage their own resourcefulness to progress in the race.

According to the BBC, the official line-up features Brit award-winning singer Ella Eyre and her childhood friend Nana, sports broadcaster Jeff Stelling and his son Matt, influencer Princess Andre with her musician brother Junior Andre, and singer Sam Ryder with his tour manager Kaz. The series, produced by Studio Lambert, is set to air on BBC One and BBC iPlayer.

The broadcaster teased the line-up with images of the contestants being photobombed by wild animals. The show is expected to start later this year, with no VIP treatment for any of the participants during their journey.

article.headline: SASSA Flags 169,000 Social Grant Beneficiaries for Potential Fraudulent Transactions
article.summary: The South African Social Security Agency has flagged 169,000 beneficiaries for further investigation after they failed to appear for mandatory grant reviews.
article.body:
A total of 169,000 grant recipients ignored notices to appear for eligibility reviews, resulting in their accounts being marked for potential fraud investigations. This massive audit is part of a wider effort by the South African Social Security Agency (SASSA) to verify the status of 352,000 beneficiaries throughout the 2026/27 financial year.

These reviews serve as a critical gatekeeper for public funds, ensuring that assistance reaches only those currently entitled to it. For many recipients, failing to update contact details or neglecting the 90-day review window risks an immediate loss of financial support. While the agency aims to prevent waste, the scale of the flagged cases underscores the difficulty in maintaining accurate beneficiary records across the country.

Minister of Social Development Dina Pule stated that these investigations address instances where eligibility has changed, cases of payments continuing after a beneficiary’s death, and accounts linked to untraceable individuals. In the first quarter alone, SASSA reviewed 105,600 files. Of those, 56,807 grants were initially suspended due to non-compliance, though 5,231 of those cases were later reinstated once the recipients complied with the verification requirements.

Risk-based data analysis continues for the remainder of the fiscal year, with specific targets set for each province. SASSA officials confirmed that while Child Support Grant reviews were prioritized in the first batch, further assessments regarding Disability and Older Persons Grants are currently being determined.

article.headline: Victorian scoops $1.2m TattsLotto win leaving the dentist
article.summary: A Strathbogie Shire man in Victoria won $1,247,390.16 in TattsLotto draw 4715 on Saturday, September 26, after purchasing his ticket from Euroa News and Lotto, learning of his win when an official called while he was driving home from a dental appointment.
article.body:
A Victorian's trip to the dentist turned into a life-changing moment when The Lott called to inform him he had won $1,247,390.16 in Saturday's TattsLotto draw 4715. The shock left him momentarily speechless as he drove home, barely able to believe the news.

The win means significant changes ahead for the man and his family. He plans to help out relatives and purchase a four-wheel drive, though he acknowledged the windfall left him overwhelmed. "I've always dreamt of all the things I'd do if I ever won but it's quite funny, now I feel stumped," he said, deciding to take a few weeks before committing to spending plans.

The winning ticket was a 10-game entry purchased from Euroa News and Lotto on Binney Street in Euroa, about 160 kilometers northeast of Melbourne. Store owner Lorraine Mawson said the sale marked a major milestone. "We're absolutely ecstatic. The last time we sold a division one-winning entry was in 2018," she said. The man was one of five division one winners in the draw, each receiving the same prize amount from the Saturday, September 26 draw.

article.headline: Code-hopper Nawaqanitawase plays final NRL match in Roosters grand final against Knights
article.summary: Sydney Roosters winger Mark Nawaqanitawase will play his last rugby league game in Sunday's grand final against Newcastle Knights before returning to rugby union and the Wallabies.
article.body:
Mark Nawaqanitawase arrived at the Roosters after the Paris 2024 Olympics and made an immediate impact, scoring a try in his round 27 debut and becoming one of the best wingers in the game within two years. But the transition from rugby union to league was mentally brutal: during his first off-season, NRL legend Andrew Johns recalled that Nawaqanitawase confessed he was questioning whether he could continue. "I don't think I can get through it," he told Johns, describing days spent training in the morning before collapsing on the lounge, unable to move. "We train in the morning, and if we have time off I just go home and lay on the lounge. I can't move off the lounge."

By his second year, Nawaqanitawase had adapted completely. When Johns saw him again, the star had adjusted to league's different fitness demands and cemented himself as a genuine superstar. Johns noted the transformation: "my body is used to it now," Nawaqanitawase told him.

Nawaqanitawase's departure marks a significant loss for the Roosters and the NRL. His return to rugby union comes with an eye on representing the Wallabies at the home Rugby World Cup next year. Interestingly, his mother Fiona Tovehi initially "tormented" her son about his move to league, but has now changed her stance and does not want him to leave the NRL.

article.headline: Wike urges Nigeria to vote for leaders sustaining Abuja's infrastructure drive
article.summary: FCT Minister Nyesom Wike called on Nigerians to elect progressive leaders in 2027 who will sustain infrastructure development in Abuja, describing the capital as a symbol of national unity.
article.body:
Nigeria's Federal Capital Territory Minister Nyesom Wike has called on residents to use the 2027 general elections to vote for leaders capable of sustaining and expanding infrastructure development in Abuja. Wike made the appeal in an Independence Day message marking Nigeria's 66th anniversary, urging voters to choose progressive and visionary leaders who will continue transforming the capital into a world-class city.

The push reflects the administration's focus on infrastructure as central to the capital's future. Wike said the FCT Administration had invested heavily in critical infrastructure, including road construction, drainage systems and solar streetlights, extending development beyond the city centre to remote rural communities. According to him, these projects aim to improve accessibility and address security challenges in communities located far from the city centre.

Wike also emphasized Abuja's symbolic importance to Nigeria. He described the capital as a reflection of national unity, where people from different ethnic, religious and cultural backgrounds live and work together. The minister said the FCT, as the nation's capital, has a responsibility to promote inclusive development and reflect the ideals of a united Nigeria.

The administration's development agenda extends beyond central Abuja to satellite towns and rural areas, with Wike stressing that residents across the territory should benefit from government projects and services. He said the FCT remains committed to creating a modern, inclusive and functional capital that serves all residents.

article.headline: Singapore watchdog busts 45 businesses, fake review provider fabricating customer ratings
article.summary: Singapore's Competition and Consumer Commission took action against a fake review provider and 45 businesses that purchased fake reviews through websites offering S$1 to S$2 per review, marking the regulator's largest investigation of this kind.
article.body:
Julian Tung Yan Kai operated two websites—BuyReviewSG and GetReviewSG—that sold fake reviews to about 100 businesses across restaurants, medical practices, legal firms and tuition agencies. The operation involved AI-generated reviews, recruiting paid reviewers via Telegram, and providing businesses with dashboards to manage their ratings.

Fake reviews undermine consumers' ability to make informed purchasing decisions, according to the Competition and Consumer Commission of Singapore (CCS). The 45 businesses that admitted to the practice acknowledged they had engaged in unfair conduct that could mislead shoppers.

Of the 47 businesses initially investigated, 45 agreed to remove fake reviews, stop the unfair practices, and publish public apologies for six months across their websites, social media and physical locations. Companies including Burma Social, Harmony Funeral Care, Picasso Hair Boutique and The Hamper Story issued statements saying "We regret our conduct and have taken corrective measures." The fake review provider also committed to cease operations and donate proceeds from the scheme to charity. Two businesses declined to accept the commission's terms. CCS called this its largest fake review investigation to date by number of businesses involved.

article.headline: DFI seizes full control of 1,100 Starbucks across Asia, exits Maxim's partnership
article.summary: DFI Retail Group will take sole control of Starbucks operations across seven Asian markets—Singapore, Hong Kong, Macau, Thailand, Vietnam, Cambodia and Laos—and receive US$340 million in cash by ending its 50-50 joint venture with Hongkong Caterers in Maxim's Caterers.
article.body:
DFI Retail Group is dismantling a longstanding partnership to consolidate power over one of Asia's largest coffee chains. The Singapore-listed company will assume full control of more than 1,100 licensed Starbucks coffeehouses across seven markets, ending a 50-50 joint venture with Hongkong Caterers that has governed Maxim's Caterers since 1972.

The restructuring significantly streamlines DFI's portfolio. The company exits its stake in Maxim's Caterers and relinquishes ownership of international food brands including Genki Sushi, Ippudo, Shake Shack and The Cheesecake Factory, which Maxim's brought into Asia. In exchange, DFI receives approximately US$340 million in cash. Hongkong Caterers becomes the sole owner of the remaining Maxim's business, which operates more than 1,000 outlets across nine markets.

Maxim's Caterers, founded in Hong Kong in 1956 by the Wu family, became the joint venture structure in 1972 with Hongkong Caterers and the Jardine Matheson Group. DFI and Hongkong Caterers stated that day-to-day operations for both Starbucks and Maxim's businesses will remain unchanged during the transition.

The deal was announced by DFI on September 29 and is expected to complete by the end of the first quarter of 2027, subject to standard closing conditions.

article.headline: Only 26.6% of young Brits have taken meningitis B vaccine as outbreaks kill three
article.summary: Health officials warn that hundreds of thousands of eligible young people have not yet received the meningitis B vaccine despite three deaths from recent outbreaks and a one-off NHS vaccination programme launched this summer.
article.body:
Just 212,549 out of 799,840 eligible young people in the UK had received the meningitis B vaccine by September 20, leaving vast numbers unprotected as outbreaks continue. The UK Health Security Agency warned that "similar outbreaks could occur again" after three deaths resulted from meningococcal disease this year, including two in an outbreak of 21 confirmed cases around Canterbury in March 2026.

First-year university students face roughly seven times higher risk of contracting meningococcal disease than young people the same age who do not attend university, according to the UK Health Security Agency. The close contact during freshers' week—from shared accommodation to socialising in pubs and clubs—creates ideal conditions for bacteria spread. Meningococcal disease can develop rapidly and become life-threatening within hours, potentially causing meningitis, sepsis, hearing loss, neurological damage and limb amputation in survivors.

Tiff O'Connor, who contracted meningitis B in her first year at university eight years ago, described the sudden onset of the disease. "My head was a pain that I'd never experienced before," she said. "I truly thought it was going to melt out of my ears." Doctors said her prior vaccination bought her crucial time. She was rushed to intensive care, put into a medically induced coma and treated with ice to lower her temperature while her family were told to say goodbye.

Year 13 pupils and individuals under 25 starting university can access two doses of the MenB vaccine via high street pharmacies and the NHS website. Health officials urged eligible individuals to book both doses as soon as possible, noting that while uptake is "gradually increasing", the large numbers remaining unprotected pose continued risk.

article.headline: Taran Armstrong Dagger Clinches 84-82 JackJumpers Thriller Over Melbourne United
article.summary: Burnie-born Taran Armstrong drilled a game-winning jump shot with 5.5 seconds remaining to secure a two-point victory for the Tasmania JackJumpers on Thursday night.
article.body: Burnie-born point guard Taran Armstrong delivered a clutch pull-up jumper with just 5.5 seconds remaining to break an 82-82 deadlock at Hobart's MyState Bank Arena. After Melbourne United’s Sam Waardenburg hit a three-pointer to level the score with 14.2 seconds on the clock, Tasmania responded with a time-out before Armstrong’s decisive shot. United had a final opportunity to steal the game, but Malith Machar’s long-range attempt rimmed out, leaving the home side victorious.  The result marks a significant defensive hold for Tasmania, which maintained its unbeaten record on home soil in NBL27. For Melbourne, the loss serves as a rare setback on a Thursday night, a time slot where the team has historically dominated with 23 wins in its last 24 appearances. article.headline: Reserve Bank surcharge ban ends extra card fees on retail purchases
article.summary: New Reserve Bank of Australia reforms effective October 1 prohibit extra checkout fees on credit, debit, and prepaid card transactions.
article.body:
While consumers no longer face added fees at checkout, some merchants are responding by raising base prices, as reported by PerthNow. For instance, one cafe owner in Perth lifted the price of a 12-ounce coffee from $6 to $6.50 following the mandate, noting that bank charges remain a cost for businesses to absorb or pass on. The Reserve Bank estimates that consumers previously paid $1.6 billion annually in surcharges, and it forecasts that lower merchant processing costs will eventually flow through to final prices.

The reform is significant because it aims to provide price certainty, ensuring that the sticker price displayed is the amount a customer pays. As noted by the SMH, the ban covers major networks including Visa, Mastercard, Eftpos, and American Express. Businesses are now required to disable surcharge functions on payment terminals and remove any existing notices about additional card fees from their stores.

According to the ABC, banks are simultaneously reducing interchange fees—the costs paid between banks—to a flat 0.3 per cent for consumer credit cards and lowering ceilings for debit and prepaid cards. As banks seek to recoup lost revenue, financial expert Nicole Pedersen-McKinnon warns that cardholders may see changes to reward points, increased annual fees, and the removal of perks like complimentary travel insurance. Banks are required to notify customers of these product updates directly.

While payment providers have disabled surcharge functions on most terminals, the SMH reports that some older machines may not update automatically, potentially delaying the removal of surcharges at specific locations.

article.headline: Sperm whale smashes yacht hull, forcing four sailors into desperate sea rescue
article.summary: Four sailors were rescued after their 52-foot yacht, the Tai Tam, sank following a collision with a pod of sperm whales in the South Pacific.
article.body:
The impact was powerful enough to knock Australian Jemma Cooper from the steering wheel of the 52-foot Tai Tam yacht as a pod of six to eight sperm whales surrounded the vessel. Crew member Jeremy Cooper recalled the terrifying moment the boat was shoved sideways, followed by the sight of brown water and several whales lingering near their damaged ship. The collision occurred 250 to 500 nautical miles off the coast of New Zealand, leaving the yacht with a compromised fiberglass structure, shattered steering gear, and water rapidly flooding the hull. 

For the four individuals aboard, the incident meant an immediate shift from sailing to a survival mission on the open ocean. After activating an emergency beacon at 1 p.m. New Zealand time on Saturday, the crew spent several hours frantically bailing water to keep the vessel afloat. The Royal New Zealand Air Force deployed a P-8A Poseidon patrol plane to coordinate the response, while the crew eventually abandoned their sinking yacht for a life raft. 

Survival on the high seas lasted 18 hours until a passing container ship successfully retrieved the group. French crew member Martin Jaffre noted that the loss of steering made the boat unmanageable, sealing its fate as it eventually went under. Despite the harrowing experience of being stranded in a life raft after their ship was destroyed, the Cooper couple has already expressed their intention to return to sailing. The rescue operation highlights the extreme danger posed by deep-sea encounters with marine wildlife, turning a routine transit into a life-or-death crisis in the remote South Pacific.

article.summary: Professional golfer Phil Mickelson voluntarily sought treatment for family trauma and addiction following recent misconduct allegations and personal health issues.
article.body: The 56-year-old golf champion recently entered and completed a stint at an addiction treatment center to address complex personal challenges. A representative for Mickelson confirmed the decision to seek professional help for both addiction and family trauma, noting that the golfer has already been discharged from the facility. This clinical intervention follows a difficult year that saw his private life thrust into the public eye through a series of professional absences and external claims regarding his conduct. In February, Mickelson announced his departure from competition, later clarifying in April that he would miss the Masters tournament to prioritize a family health matter. His representatives maintained in June that his primary focus remains on his role as a husband and father. The decision to enter treatment comes after multiple allegations surfaced against the athlete, including claims by a female golf course employee who reported nonconsensual physical contact. Additionally, Ashley Perez alleged that Mickelson made inappropriate sexual gestures toward her in 2015. Mickelson has publicly labeled these reports as a misleading narrative and described the allegations as a drive-by shooting, while his wife, Amy, has expressed her support throughout the period. Mickelson has previously spoken openly about his history with gambling, admitting in 2023 that his habits had shifted from moderate to addictive, which significantly impacted his personal life.
